name: CKD G3-G5 (not on dialysis): protein about 0.8 g/kg
rationale: For adults with moderate to advanced kidney disease who are not on dialysis, protein is kept at about 0.8 g per kg body weight a day.
source_locator: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of CKD, Kidney Int 2024;105(4S):S117-S314 (PMID 38490803), Chapter 3, diet section. DRAFT: recommendation numbers not confirmed; values from KDIGO's own patient takeaways PDF and the NephJC review.

name: CKD adults: avoid very high protein
rationale: Avoid protein above 1.3 g per kg body weight a day in kidney disease that may progress.
source_locator: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of CKD, Kidney Int 2024;105(4S):S117-S314 (PMID 38490803), Chapter 3, diet section. DRAFT: recommendation numbers not confirmed; values from KDIGO's own patient takeaways PDF and the NephJC review. Practice Point 3.3.2 (ungraded).

name: CKD: sodium below 2 g a day
rationale: Keep sodium below 2,000 mg a day (about 5 g of salt) to help control blood pressure and fluid.
source_locator: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of CKD, Kidney Int 2024;105(4S):S117-S314 (PMID 38490803), Chapter 3, diet section. DRAFT: recommendation numbers not confirmed; values from KDIGO's own patient takeaways PDF and the NephJC review.

name: CKD: sodium ceiling
rationale: Sodium should stay below 2,300 mg a day in kidney disease.
source_locator: KDOQI Clinical Practice Guideline for Nutrition in CKD: 2020 Update, Am J Kidney Dis 2020;76(3 Suppl 1):S1-S107. DRAFT: values taken from published summaries/tables, primary text not read.

name: CKD: potassium limit set by the clinician
rationale: Potassium must be matched to your blood potassium level; your kidney team sets the daily limit.
source_locator: KDOQI Clinical Practice Guideline for Nutrition in CKD: 2020 Update, Am J Kidney Dis 2020;76(3 Suppl 1):S1-S107. DRAFT: values taken from published summaries/tables, primary text not read. The guideline gives NO fixed intake: adjust dietary potassium to keep serum potassium in the normal range. The numeric limit must come from the patient's clinician.

name: CKD: phosphorus limit set by the clinician
rationale: Phosphorus must be matched to your blood phosphate level; your kidney team sets the daily limit.
source_locator: KDOQI Clinical Practice Guideline for Nutrition in CKD: 2020 Update, Am J Kidney Dis 2020;76(3 Suppl 1):S1-S107. DRAFT: values taken from published summaries/tables, primary text not read. The guideline gives NO fixed intake: adjust dietary phosphorus to keep serum phosphate in the normal range. The numeric limit must come from the patient's clinician.

name: Dialysis: do not auto-plan
rationale: On dialysis your protein, potassium, phosphorus, sodium and fluid targets are set by your kidney team and differ from the general rules.
source_locator: KDOQI Clinical Practice Guideline for Nutrition in CKD: 2020 Update, Am J Kidney Dis 2020;76(3 Suppl 1):S1-S107. DRAFT: values taken from published summaries/tables, primary text not read. (dialysis protein/energy ranges differ; planning must be clinician-directed).

name: CKD: dietitian-guided, plant-forward, low in ultra-processed foods
rationale: A kidney dietitian should individualise sodium, potassium, phosphorus and protein; favour plant-based foods and limit ultra-processed foods.
source_locator: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of CKD, Kidney Int 2024;105(4S):S117-S314 (PMID 38490803), Chapter 3, diet section. DRAFT: recommendation numbers not confirmed; values from KDIGO's own patient takeaways PDF and the NephJC review. Practice Point 3.3.1 and renal-dietitian practice point.
